title: IBRANCE (palbociclib): Patient Support Programs and Practical Tools
summary: Pfizer offers a comprehensive patient support ecosystem for IBRANCE (palbociclib) branded "Pfizer Oncology Together," encompassing co-pay savings cards for commercially insured patients, a free Patient Assistance Program for uninsured/underinsured patients, trial vouchers for new starts, benefits verification and prior authorization/appeals support for HCP offices, and non-financial "Care Champion" navigation services (transportation, lodging, counseling referrals, and educational materials). Administration and monitoring aids include structured dosing/CBC monitoring schedules embedded in the FDA label and reinforced through Pfizer HCP and patient-facing tools (e.g., a downloadable dosing tracker), reflecting the label's core requirement of complete blood count monitoring at baseline, Day 15 of cycles 1–2, and each subsequent cycle start. All financial program details (amounts, eligibility) are drawn from Pfizer/Pfizer Oncology Together promotional and program materials rather than the FDA label, and terms are stated to be subject to change; several sourced figures for the co-pay program's annual maximum are inconsistent across Pfizer's own pages (ranging from $4,000–$10,000 up to $25,000/$10,600 depending on page and date), which should be flagged as a gap requiring verification against the current official terms and conditions at the time of clinical use.

claims.text: Pfizer offers Pfizer Oncology Together, a program providing personalized support and free services to patients and caregivers throughout treatment for HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer with IBRANCE, including help identifying financial assistance options and connecting patients/caregivers to day-to-day support resources.

claims.text: Eligible, commercially insured patients may pay as little as $0 per month for their IBRANCE prescription through the Pfizer Oncology Together Co-Pay Savings Program; stated annual savings caps vary across official Pfizer pages, with figures cited as $4,000–$10,000, $10,600 per product, and up to $25,000 depending on the specific program page and version accessed.

claims.text: Complete blood count (CBC) monitoring is the only scheduled laboratory monitoring requirement in the current FDA-approved IBRANCE Prescribing Information; ECG, serum electrolyte, or liver enzyme testing are not required by label. Recommended CBC schedule: prior to starting therapy, on Days 1 and 15 of the first 2 cycles, on Day 1 of subsequent cycles, and as clinically indicated; monitoring frequency may decrease to every 3 months (prior to cycle start) for patients with no more than Grade 1-2 neutropenia during the first 6 cycles.

claims.text: IBRANCE patient education (label-derived) instructs patients to take their dose at approximately the same time each day, that capsules must always be taken with food while tablets may be taken with or without food, and that tablets/capsules should be swallowed whole and not chewed, crushed, opened, or split, nor ingested if broken or cracked; if a dose is vomited or missed, an additional dose should not be taken that day and the next scheduled dose should be taken as usual.

citations.title: Dosing & Administration | IBRANCE® (palbociclib)
citations.supporting_text: IBRANCE capsules should always be taken with food. Patients should be encouraged to take their dose at approximately the same time each day. If the patient vomits or misses a dose, an additional dose should not be taken that day.

citations.title: Dosing & Administration | IBRANCE® (palbociclib)
citations.supporting_text: IBRANCE tablets and capsules should be swallowed whole (patients should not chew, crush, open, or split them prior to swallowing). Tablets and capsules should not be ingested if they are broken, cracked, or otherwise not intact.

claims.text: Patient-facing education materials advise avoiding grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and grapefruit products during IBRANCE therapy because they may increase blood levels of the drug, and suggest practical adherence aids such as setting a phone/watch reminder and tracking treatment days on a calendar; a downloadable 'Dosing Tracker' is offered to help patients track IBRANCE and fulvestrant dosing schedules.

gaps: Pfizer's own program pages list materially different annual co-pay savings caps for the IBRANCE Co-Pay Savings Program (variously $4,000-$10,000, $10,600 per product, and up to $25,000) depending on the specific page/version and access date; the current, single authoritative cap should be confirmed directly at PfizerOncologyTogether.com/terms at time of use rather than relying on any one cached figure.

Exact income eligibility threshold (e.g., % of Federal Poverty Level) for the Pfizer Patient Assistance Program specific to IBRANCE was not located in the primary sources retrieved; general Pfizer RxPathways materials cite thresholds (300-400% FPL) for other/multiple products but a IBRANCE-specific FPL cutoff was not confirmed.

No FDA-approved digital therapeutic, official Pfizer mobile app, or dedicated adherence app specific to IBRANCE was identified in the search results beyond a downloadable PDF 'Dosing Tracker' on ibrance.com; presence/absence of an official Pfizer mobile app should be treated as unconfirmed.

Independent charitable foundation assistance (e.g., PAN Foundation) figures and availability are subject to frequent change and periodic fund closures; the $2,400/year figure for breast cancer from GoodRx (secondary source) should be independently verified against the foundation's own current disease-fund page, which was not directly queried in this research.

Precise, current phone numbers/URLs for Pfizer Oncology Together (e.g., 1-877-744-5675 vs. 1-844-9-IBRANCE) appear on different pages for different purposes (general support vs. co-pay card) and should be verified as still active/correct at time of clinical reference.
warnings: Financial assistance amounts, eligibility rules, and voucher expiration dates are promotional program terms set by Pfizer and are explicitly subject to change or rescission without notice per Pfizer's own disclosures; these are not FDA-approved label content and should not be treated as fixed or guaranteed.

Several cited pages are Pfizer HCP-facing (pfizerpro.com) marketing/promotional pages that intermix clinical safety information with program details; while useful for identifying available support services, program terms should be confirmed against the official Terms and Conditions page before being communicated to patients.

Some search results are third-party aggregator/comparison sites (e.g., PrescriberPoint, NowPatient, Simplefill, GoodRx) that explicitly disclaim manufacturer verification of their content; figures from these sources are noted as lower-confidence and were only used where no conflicting primary source was available, and should be corroborated independently.

One secondary source (Simplefill) referenced an expired copay card program end-date (December 31, 2022) alongside a distinct $25,000 maximum figure, indicating that some cached/aggregator content may be outdated; only current, dated primary sources should be relied upon for patient-facing counseling.
